label: copy-phase input of j/u (also n, 0, 1), rare sparse subset
explanation: Fires almost only in the copy phase (99% of mass), when the token fed back in is j (49% of mass), u (23%), n, 0 or 1. Those five input tokens account for ~99% of activations. Even so it is very sparse: it fires on only ~0.1-0.2% of the steps that match, so precision is tiny (~0.1%). It is enriched in long sequences (L=9 holds 73% of mass), early in recall (recall_idx 1-3, to_go 5-7) and when the output token is also j/u/0/1. Stacking those conditions raises precision only to ~5% and costs most of the recall, so the real trigger depends on something these variables do not capture. The strongest activations are on j/u inputs at recall_idx 0-2 of L=9 sequences. Activations are small and uniform (mean 0.12, max 0.17). It never fires in the original phase (4 stray steps) or on <DEL>, and does not fire on other letters.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues.
